_provenance: HAND LABELS. Made by the project owner on 2026-09-15 by watching label-rally-A.mp4 and label-rally-B.mp4 -- the working video at a third speed with its frame numbers burned in and no pipeline output drawn on it -- and written as one line per contact in labels.tsv, which is kept beside this file as the primary record. Every contact carries a hitter; none was left unattributed. The hitters alternate strictly across both spans, which is what singles requires and which no labelling produced here before had achieved.
_supersedes: Model-produced labels for the same two spans, written by Claude on 2026-09-15 and kept at git f7e7a81. They were made without sight of these, and comparing the two measures how far model labelling can be trusted: contact precision 0.829 and recall 0.763, hitter accuracy 0.864 over the 22 contacts the model was willing to name. The model missed 9 contacts, invented 6, and named the wrong player 3 times. Seven of the nine frames it recorded as detector false positives were real contacts it had itself missed.
_labelling_caveats: One weak anchor: before labelling began the labeller had been told the model found "~35 contacts". That is an anchor on the total, not on positions or hitters. The hand count came to 38.
The notes carry a shot type for most contacts -- serve, lift, drive, net, smash, clear, drop. Nothing in milestone 1 reads them; they are gold data for milestone 2 if it resumes.

Only the two spans in labelled_contact_spans are exhaustive. Rallies are labelled across the whole clip and were carried over unchanged from the earlier pass, where they rest on the scoreboard reading 3-7 at frames 200, 480, 900 and 960 and 3-8 by 1020.
_rally_labelling_note: The rally spans were wrong in the first pass and are corrected here. Seven were claimed; the clip holds five. The instrument that settled it is the scoreboard, which runs 3-7, 3-8, 3-9, 4-9, 4-10, 4-11 across the clip -- five points, five rallies -- and not the shuttle track, from which the first pass had derived them by taking every run of moving shuttle for a rally. Two of those runs are players knocking the shuttle back between points. Ends are the frame the shuttle comes to rest, read off the raw track. Three automatic rules for that were tried first and each failed differently: the first standstill runs late because a grounded shuttle jitters up to 31 px, sustained-travel runs late for the same reason and cuts rallies short at blind gaps, and both are confounded by the tracker leaping onto its parked point, which looks like motion.
_shot_type_provenance: Shot types are the labeller's own words, recorded in labels.tsv at the same time as the contacts and lifted into shot_type here without reinterpretation. Two notes named more than one shot and were resolved by the labeller on 2026-09-15: 1851 is a net shot played defensively against a smash, and 2090 is a lift. Nothing in Milestone 1 reads this field.
